references.title: Grand Theft Auto VI understands just how important a smartphone is
references.excerpt: Grand Theft Auto VI, in many ways, tries to simulate real life. And life in 2026 would not be complete without a smartphone. GTA VI understands this and makes the phone not just a central part of the experience, but an object that exists within the world. You may try to escape into a fantasy of robbing banks and fighting drug lords, but you can't get away from texts from your mom or nagging fitness app notifications. Seeing a smartphone in a game isn't a new phenomenon. The device has become a natural stand-in for the main menu in many games, giving players an interface that feels intuitive, because a phone is something they use every day. …

references.title: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks
references.excerpt: Was it worth it? I've been asking myself this quite a bit over the last month or so while testing both the Amazon Bee Frontier and Siri Recap on the Apple Watch Ultra 4. The main difference is that Amazon's Bee takes a maximalist (and frankly reality-bending) approach, whereas Apple is going for a more minimalist, privacy-first take. references.title: Blue Origin will launch Google’s AI server satellites in 2029
references.excerpt: Google is teaming up with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch its AI server satellites. The companies announced on Thursday that Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will shuttle satellites equipped with Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) into space in the first quarter of 2029. The partnership is part of Google's Project Suncatcher, a moonshot plan that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google deployed its first AI server satellite in October, successfully booting up its TPUs and using the onboard Gemma 4 model to transmit an AI-generated haiku to Earth.
